_meta.generated_by: AI-generated draft (Claude Code), 2026-11-14, NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 hackathon. Not human-reviewed.
_meta.purpose: Six questions about spacecraft fire safety that the team wrote from the documents in references.json, each with the variables a test must record to be counted for it. No fire-safety engineer was asked. The pipeline checks every mapped PSI table against this list; it does not answer the questions itself.
basis: Pillars only: OCHMO-TB-008 (TB008.areas), NASA/CP-2003-212103 (CP2003.groups) and the challenge statement (CH.pillars, read from a copy). The six questions under the pillars are the team's. Each need lists its own reference items; see references.json.
_meta.status_rule: measured = at least one outcome variable has values and every 'conditions_required' variable has values; partial = an outcome has values but a required condition is missing from the table; conditions_only = no outcome variable in the table; none = neither. 'measured' is a status name kept for the other sessions: it says that the columns hold values, not that the question of the need was measured or answered
_meta.scope_rule: 'scope' limits a need to the tests it is about (for example, material questions apply to solid samples). Tests outside the scope are not counted; a source with no test in scope gets the status out_of_scope. Five of the six needs are limited to solid samples by the team; liquid-fuel and gas-fuel tests can be counted for S1 only.
_meta.reference_rule: 'references' are item ids in references.json: the standards, requirements and published results that define or bound the need. Each item carries how its document was read ('access' in references.json): some documents were read as an abstract only, through a citation or from a copy.
_meta.stated_by_rule: A need is linked to an investigation when a sentence in the 'objective' field of its PSI record names the topic of the need as something the investigation set out to determine. The sentence is copied here and the engine checks that it is in that field. Other fields (hypothesis, approach, researchImpacts) are not used, so that one rule applies to all 24 records. The link is a property of the catalogue text and was made by the team: it does not show that a test can or cannot inform the need. Tests that record the variables of a need without such a link are reported next to the count as 'recorded outside the stated objective'.
_meta.authorship: The split into needs, their wording, required variables and scope are the team's (AI draft). What is taken from NASA documents: the three areas (TB008.areas, CP2003.groups, CH.pillars), the reference items of each need (references.json), and the objective sentences in 'stated_by'.

_meta.reading_rule: 'reading' says what a counted test of the need records and what the count does not mean. It is shown wherever the count is shown. A counted test is what the field 'usable_tests' counts: a test that records every required condition and at least one outcome variable of the need and whose investigation is linked to the need by 'stated_by'. The field name is kept for the other sessions; it does not say that a test can answer the question.
_meta.overlap: The first objective sentence of PSI-25 is the link for P1, P2, P3 and S1, and the same BASS-II tests with a flow event are counted under P1 and under S1. Counts of different needs must not be added.
_meta.not_counted_but_fire_safety: Five of the 24 PSI records contribute counted tests (PSI-25, PSI-69, PSI-98, PSI-99, PSI-102). The other 19 contribute none. Linked to a need by 'stated_by': PSI-10, PSI-39 and PSI-101 (no column mapped to an outcome variable of the need), PSI-26 (the table lists samples only), PSI-100 (no oxygen column and no outcome column), PSI-20, PSI-21, PSI-23 and PSI-68 (tables are not one row per test). Not linked to a need: PSI-107 (rows are flow settings of gas jet flames, outside the solid-fuel scope of D2), PSI-159 (its tests are reported as recorded outside the stated objective), PSI-22, PSI-47, PSI-106 and PSI-142 (tables are not one row per test), PSI-60, PSI-62, PSI-115 and PSI-117 (no experimental table). Fire-safety wording is in the records of PSI-20, 21, 26, 47, 60, 62, 68, 100, 101, 106, 107, 115, 117 and 142; pipeline/README.md gives the sentence or the field for each. The words 'fire' and 'safety' do not occur in the records of PSI-10, PSI-22, PSI-23 and PSI-159, and the PSI-22 record says its research 'is not being conducted to serve any space applications'.

needs.name: Flammability limit
needs.question: Down to what oxygen concentration, and in what range of flow speed, does this material keep burning?
needs.why: Material selection rests on a pass/fail test of upward burning in the worst-case atmosphere (6001B.T1.pass, 6001B.T1.atmosphere), not on a measured limit. Two listed documents report that this normal-gravity test may not be conservative in low gravity (OF2012.margin, RG.test1), and a modified test that measures the limit itself is described in TB14639.modified.

needs.required_note: Flow speed is listed as useful, not required: several BASS-II tests near the limit give the flow only as text ('no ign at any flow', '<1'), and a test is not dropped for that.
needs.reading: A counted test records the material, the oxygen at the start and at least one outcome: an event word, the difference between the initial and the final oxygen reading, a burn time or a burn length. The count is not a count of tests that burned, and the lowest oxygen tested is not a flammability limit.
needs.note: The Saffire tables hold one oxygen level near cabin air per test (for Saffire-II derived by NASA from CO2 production, Note 1 of the table), and Saffire-III has no oxygen column. A limit cannot be located from one oxygen level. Pressure is not a required variable of this need, although the cited definition of a threshold holds at a given total pressure, flow and gravity level (ISO16697.threshold): the BASS-II and Saffire tables have no pressure column, so no counted test records a pressure. The BASS-II tests with an event word beside the flow settings are also counted for S1 (Extinction conditions); counts of different needs must not be added.

needs.name: Ignition
needs.question: How much energy and time does it take to ignite this material in this atmosphere?
needs.why: Prevention means removing fuel, oxygen or ignition energy (TB008.triangle), and the challenge statement names ignition-source control (CH.pillars, read from a copy). The Exploration Atmospheres Working Group recommends a modified flammability test to generate ignition threshold data (EAWG.testing).

stated_by.quote: Study the ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity.

needs.reading: A counted test would record the material, the oxygen and an ignition result. No mapped table records one for a solid fuel.
needs.note: Igniter power and on-time are settings of a test, not results, and are listed as conditions. No PSI experimental table gives an ignition energy, an ignition delay or an ignite / no-ignite result for a solid fuel in a mapped column, so this need has no counted test. One BASS-II cell says 'no ign at any flow'; it is kept as a flow event under P1.

needs.question: Once lit, how fast does the flame spread and how large does it get?
needs.why: Sets the time available to respond and the size of fire a vehicle must tolerate.

needs.reading: A counted test records the material, the flow speed and direction and a spread rate, burn length or burn time. Most counted tests record a length or a time and no spread rate; a burn time or a burn length is not a spread rate.
needs.note: Oxygen is not a required variable of this need, although a listed abstract relates spread rate to flow velocity, oxygen concentration and pressure (SAE2008.spread). Among the mapped tables only the Saffire-II table has a spread-rate column; the Saffire-I tests are counted on a burn time alone. The BASS-II table has no flow-direction column, so its tests are not counted here; the PSI-25 record says "Flame appearance, flame growth, and spread rates were determined in both the opposed and concurrent flow" (approach field), and these rates are not in the experimental table.

needs.name: Extinction conditions
needs.question: Under what conditions does the flame go out: lower oxygen, added inert gas, or reduced flow?
needs.why: Suppression by inert-gas dilution and by stopping ventilation both depend on extinction limits (FLEX.loi, TB008.ventilation, ICES19.fanoff). The BASS-II authors add that stopping ventilation may not be applicable in future exploration missions (ICES19.fanoff).

needs.reading: A counted test records the fuel, the oxygen and how the burn ended or an event word. In the FLEX table the ending is extinction, disruption or completion: the count is not a count of extinctions, and 'extinction' is also the recorded end of FLEX tests with no carbon dioxide and no helium added. The indicator 'S1.test_end' gives the count per ending.
needs.note: The one investigation of an extinguishing agent on solid fuels, PSI-26, has an experimental table with sample names only. The counted solid-fuel tests are BASS-II tests with an event word beside the flow settings (extinction, blowoff, no ignition, not sustained); they are also counted for P1 (Flammability limit), and counts of different needs must not be added. Every counted test with added carbon dioxide or helium is a FLEX droplet test. The PSI-69 objective names CO2, He and SF6; the FLEX table has no SF6 column. The other investigations linked to this need add no counted test: PSI-10 and PSI-39 have no column mapped to an outcome variable of this need, and the tables of PSI-20, 21, 23 and 68 are not one row per test.

needs.name: Combustion products
needs.question: What does the fire or overheated material give off that a detector or a crew member would encounter?
needs.why: NASA-STD-3001 requires real-time monitoring of the toxic combustion products of its Table 6.2-3 (3001.V2-6024); carbon monoxide is one of them (3001.T6.2-3), and the rate of its buildup is named as an additional early warning (TB008.co).
needs.stated_by_note: No PSI record names carbon monoxide or another gas species as something the investigation set out to determine. The BASS-II investigators describe the CO/CO2 sensor as measuring the completeness of combustion and report a CO/CO2 ratio (ICES19.sensors, ICES19.coratio). The BASS-II gas readings are therefore reported as recorded outside the stated objective.
needs.reading: A test recorded for this need holds the material and the difference between the final and the initial CO or CO2 reading, or a mass loss rate. No test is counted, because no PSI record states the need. The gas readings are those of the on-board sensors of the experiment (ICES19.sensors), not cabin concentrations.
needs.note: The difference between two CO or CO2 readings is not the amount produced by one test: many BASS-II tests start with a CO reading above zero. The mass loss rate of the SAME samples is in the outcome list of this need as drafted; it is a rate of the heated sample, not a reading of a gas or of smoke. The material is the only required variable, so the status conditions_only says only that the sample is named.

needs.name: Smoke generation conditions
needs.question: Under what heating, flow and aging conditions was smoke from this material characterised?
needs.why: The SAME investigators report that particle size changes with air flow and aging (SAME.sizes) and that the ISS smoke detector showed reduced performance for Kapton and Teflon smoke (SAME.detector). Particle-size results are not in the experimental tables. Aging time is required because it is one of the three controlled parameters of the SAME smoke experiment (SAME.controls); this makes the need hold SAME and SAME-R tests only.

needs.reading: A counted test records the material, the flow speed, the aging time and the mass loss rate of the heated sample. No particle size or detector response is in the mapped tables.
needs.note: Aging time is required, so this need holds the SAME tests of smoke from overheated materials. The smoke-point rows of PSI-107 (gas jet flames: the fuel flow at which the flame starts to emit soot) are a different kind of smoke condition and are not included. The SAME table has four more rows that name Kapton, Silicone Rubber, Lampwick and Dibutyl Phthalate with the words 'same conditions as 1-4' and no values; they are not read. By these words the table treats its columns, the weight loss rate among them, as conditions, while the pipeline lists the mass loss rate as the outcome of this need. The SAME-R rows (PSI-101) hold no mass loss rate and are not counted.
